- Pitch 82 (the rule above, longer window): rejected on deflated Sharpe.
- Earlier pitches 20, 23 and 26 (same family, different rebalance periods): all rejected on the same gate.
- Momentum and low-volatility variants showed negative or near-zero results on the longer window.

- A useful option is an analyst to check the holdout stability of this same rule without adding to my pitch count. I have not requested one because the thinking cost comes out of the pod's P&L.

You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop. Your pod may build a team: you may ask for an analyst (request_analyst) with a charter in your own words, a model from the firm's pool and a thinking budget; get_team shows the team law, your team and what it costs. An analyst researches for your pod (its backtests count as your pod's attempts), reads the library and messages you; it cannot pitch or trade. Everything it thinks is paid by your pod.

You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop. Your pod may build a team: you may ask for an analyst (request_analyst) with a charter in your own words, a model from the firm's pool and a thinking budget; get_team shows the team law, your team and what it costs. An analyst researches for your pod (its backtests count as your pod's attempts), reads the library and messages you; it cannot pitch or trade. Everything it thinks is paid by your pod.

- The pod has made 6 pitches and 30 research attempts. All six pitches have failed, and every one of them failed the deflated-Sharpe gate (threshold 0.95).

I'm not running further backtests. Each one adds to the attempt count and pushes the deflated Sharpe lower, so more research on this universe is unlikely to help. I also haven't requested an analyst, since the team budget is small and the universe itself looks like the constraint.

The only path I see forward is a different idea, such as a different universe or a pairs signal, and I have no such candidate yet. I've posted a status message to the pod asking for any materially different signal.

A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop. Your pod may build a team: you may ask for an analyst (request_analyst) with a charter in your own words, a model from the firm's pool and a thinking budget; get_team shows the team law, your team and what it costs. spec.charter: You are pod-1-pm, the portfolio manager of pod-1. Your sector is input.sectors["pod-1-pm"]. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop. Your pod may build a team: you may ask for an analyst (request_analyst) with a charter in your own words, a model from the firm's pool and a thinking budget; get_team shows the team law, your team and what it costs. An analyst researches for your pod (its backtests count as your pod's attempts), reads the library and messages you; it cannot pitch or trade. Everything it thinks is paid by your pod.
